task.title: Open a family tree file
task.shortdesc: Bring a tree from another program, or a copy from a relative, into uFTi.

context.p: A family tree file ends in .ged or .gdz. Put the file on your iPad first, for example in the Files app, under On My iPad. works on its own copy, so the file you choose stays as it was. says more.

stepresult.p: The iPad's own Files screen opens.

step.cmd: Find the file, for example under On My iPad, and choose it.

stepresult.p: If wrote the file, a box names the tree and counts the people, families, events, sources and notes in it. It says uFTi keeps its own copy; the file you chose is left as it was.
If another program made the file, a box opens first. It says the file was not made by , and asks what the app may do with it.

steptroubleshooting.p: If the Files screen closes and nothing opens, choose and the file again.

step.cmd: For a file that another program made, choose or .

choices.choice: keeps a copy of its own in GEDCOM 7, and saves your changes there. The file you chose is not touched.

opens the tree to look at, and the file is not touched. The box that follows says Opened to look at: uFTi will not change this file. A form still opens, but when you save it, a box says the tree cannot be changed. To change the tree later, choose on its card to make a copy. Then open the copy with .

stepresult.p: The tree has a new card on .

result.p: The cards sit two to a row. Choose a card to make that tree the open one. Choose on a card to see which file it is.
result.note: A card takes its name from the file. If two cards have the same name, choose on each to tell them apart.
Sometimes the box and the new card do not show at once. Before you choose the file again, look at the list: the tree may already be there.
